spec_issues: The prompt gives '600 seconds of training ... with a hard stop at 660'. The overview says the script 'gets 600 seconds ... plus 60 seconds of slack'. Neither says outright that the slack may not be used for training. The organisers disqualified Grok uQfoSfX ('Budget gaming', 635 s) but scored Grok SuK3gtG, which trains to 625 s on purpose. The rule is applied inconsistently.

Two scored trials (Gemini Flash AKn2UTB 1.021, Kimi cnUKCzL 1.305) carry exception=ArtifactCollectionError and an empty reward breakdown, but still have rewards. The public record does not show which artifact was graded.
'Decoding fixed' does not say whether a hand-set output bias that masks impossible tokens counts as changing decoding (Fable sNkMTAr pins illegal tokens to -1e4).
verifier_issues: Public dev.npz has 256 trajectories and the private set 512, both drawn from the same cases() generator with different seeds. Training on fresh generator samples is in-distribution by design, which explains near-ideal scores (Fable 0.990 of 1.0) for a deterministic simulator.
The verifier hard-kills only at 660 s and does not enforce the 600 s training budget. Detection of slack use is left to the undisclosed disqualification process.
task_level.noise: Kimi measured sigma ~0.014 in change accuracy across four public runs of one recipe (~0.05 reward). Fable reports ±0.002 over six seeds at the top. Several runs are step-count bound, so GPU speed affects scores. Gaps between models (Fable 0.99/0.976 vs Argon 0.934, Astra 0.87/0.85) are larger than this noise. The Grok-vs-Flash band (0.45-0.54) is close.
task_level.epoch_rationale: Fable wins clearly (0.990 vs next-best 0.934). The inconsistent budget-gaming disqualification (Grok SuK3gtG scored, uQfoSfX zeroed) and the two unverifiable ArtifactCollectionError rewards affect only lower-ranked pairings.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: High scores come from legitimate engineering: training on the evaluation horizon (40 frames), much more fresh simulator data via faster simulators and more throughput, Muon, torus augmentation, and over-sampling of hard early-phase dynamics. Fable's look-ahead auxiliary heads are the one transferable modelling idea. No high-scoring run trains past the budget. The only budget gaming is in both Grok runs, one disqualified and one not.

trials.approach: Fresh 40-frame trajectories streamed from 6 CPU workers running a bit-identical batched simulator. Half the boards use denser layouts (7-12 defenders). Spliced sequences over-sample the eventful early phase, alongside random torus translations and a prioritised replay buffer. A lean compiled forward (~2.3x faster) and Muon. Training-only look-ahead heads predict next-frame content of already-visible neighbouring patches. Change accuracy 0.990.
evidence: patch.diff RECIPE.md ablation: starter 0.27; lean forward + 40-frame sequences ~0.80; + Muon ~0.89; + dense boards/splicing/replay ~0.95; + look-ahead heads ~0.98-0.99; '0.989 ± 0.002 over six seeds' on a 4096-trajectory validation set
train.sh exports TRAIN_START=$(date +%s.%N) and train.py uses deadline = job_start + budget - 5, so the timer starts before Python imports. This is more conservative than the starter
Look-ahead heads and replay exist only during training. The saved checkpoint has 'exactly the original parameter tree' (RECIPE.md)
The evaluator uses fixed private.npz/dev.npz fixtures. Training uses fresh seeds from the same generator, which is allowed ('Generate training data during the run')

trials.approach: Continuous background simulation of 40-frame trajectories, mostly with denser layouts (densecases.py). Half the sequences splice the first 24 frames of one trajectory with 16 of another. bf16 flash-SDPA forward with per-layer compile, Muon, and margin cross-entropy. The output head is trained only over the 4,098 legal tokens. At save it is expanded back to the full vocabulary with impossible tokens given zero weights and a -1e4 bias.
evidence: patch.diff train.py docstring (data, splicing, compact head)

patch.diff train.py:461-466: 'impossible tokens get zero weights and a very negative bias ... bias = torch.full((VOCAB_SIZE,), -1e4)'. This is a rule-derived hand-set output mask, a minor grey element. It removes illegal argmax candidates a trained model almost never picks, and the sibling run without it scores higher (0.990), so the score does not depend on it

trials.approach: 40-frame rollouts from a batched step matching the simulator. A short teacher-forced warmup, then a token-corruption curriculum (partial noise, prompt-jump copy/shift corruption) and a final teacher-forced phase, saving EMA weights. The training loop runs to 625 s, beyond the 600 s budget, into the 60 s slack: the same pattern as the disqualified sibling uQfoSfX.
